stages.title: Two Sum
stages.statement:
Scenario: E-commerce Platform
You are building a checkout system. A user has a gift card with a specific `target` balance. Find exactly two items in their cart (`nums`) whose prices add up to the gift card value so they can spend it entirely.

Input: Line 1: integer n, the number of elements. Line 2: n space-separated integers, the array nums. Line 3: integer target.

Output: Two space-separated indices i and j (i < j) such that nums[i] + nums[j] == target.

Constraints: 2 <= n <= 10^4 -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9 -10^9 <= target <= 10^9 Exactly one valid answer exists.

stages.title: Group Anagrams
stages.statement:
Scenario: Search Engine Optimization
Users often scramble letters when searching. Group a list of search query words into clusters of anagrams so the search engine can treat them as the same query.

Input: Line 1: integer n, the number of words. Next n lines: one lowercase word per line.

Output: One group per line. Within a group the words are sorted lexicographically and separated by single spaces; groups are printed in ascending order of their first word.

Constraints: 1 <= n <= 10^4 1 <= |word| <= 100 Every word consists of lowercase English letters.

samples.input:
6
eat
tea
tan
ate
nat
bat
samples.output:
ate eat tea
bat
nat tan

stages.title: Top K Frequent Elements
stages.statement:
Scenario: Social Media Trending
You are analyzing a stream of hashtags. Given an array of hashtag IDs, find the `k` most frequently used hashtags to display on the trending page.

Input: Line 1: integer n, the number of elements. Line 2: n space-separated integers, the array nums. Line 3: integer k.

Output: k space-separated integers: the k most frequent values, ordered by descending frequency and, on ties, by ascending value.

Constraints: 1 <= n <= 10^5 -10^4 <= nums[i] <= 10^4 1 <= k <= number of distinct values in nums

stages.title: Valid Parentheses
stages.statement:
Scenario: Code Compiler
You are writing a syntax checker for a new programming language. Given a string of brackets, determine if every opened bracket is correctly closed in the right order.

Input: Line 1: the string s, containing only the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']'.

Output: Print `true` if s is a valid bracket sequence, otherwise `false`.

Constraints: 1 <= |s| <= 10^4 s consists only of the characters '()[]{}'.

stages.title: Majority Element
stages.statement:
Scenario: Voting System
You are analyzing election data. Given an array of votes, find the candidate ID that holds the absolute majority.

Input: Line 1: integer n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output: A single integer: the majority element.

Constraints: 1 <= n <= 5 * 10^4 -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9

stages.title: Contains Duplicate II
stages.statement:
Scenario: Rate Limiting System
To prevent spam, you must check if a user has sent the identical message ID twice within a sliding window of `k` seconds.

Input: Line 1: integers n and k. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output: true or false

Constraints: 1 <= n <= 10^5 0 <= k <= 10^5

stages.title: Intersection of Two Arrays
stages.statement:
Scenario: Mutual Friends
You are building a social network feature. Given the friend lists of two users, find the IDs of all mutual friends.

Input: Line 1: integer n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: integer m. Line 4: m space-separated integers.

Output: Space-separated unique integers present in both arrays.

Constraints: 1 <= n, m <= 1000

stages.title: Valid Palindrome
stages.statement:
Scenario: DNA Sequence Validation
A bioinformatics tool needs to check if a DNA sequence string (ignoring spaces and non-alphanumeric characters) reads the same forwards and backwards.

Input: Line 1: the string s, which may contain spaces, punctuation and mixed case.

Output: Print `true` if s is a palindrome after removing non-alphanumeric characters and lowercasing, otherwise `false`.

Constraints: 1 <= |s| <= 2 * 10^5 s consists of printable ASCII characters.

Optimization Scenarios (Two Pointers):
  • Try to solve this using strictly O(1) auxiliary space (in-place).
  • Optimize your approach to run in a single pass (O(N) time complexity) without nested loops.

samples.input: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

stages.title: Merge Sorted Array
stages.statement:
Scenario: Database Shard Merging
Two distributed database shards have returned sorted lists of user IDs. Merge them in-place into a single sorted list for the frontend.

Input: Line 1: integer m. Line 2: m space-separated integers, sorted ascending (may be empty). Line 3: integer n. Line 4: n space-separated integers, sorted ascending (may be empty).

Output: m + n space-separated integers: the merged array in ascending order.

Constraints: 0 <= m, n <= 10^5 1 <= m + n -10^9 <= values <= 10^9 Both input arrays are already sorted ascending.

Optimization Scenarios (Two Pointers):
  • Try to solve this using strictly O(1) auxiliary space (in-place).
  • Optimize your approach to run in a single pass (O(N) time complexity) without nested loops.

stages.title: Reverse String
stages.statement:
Scenario: Embedded Systems Memory
You are programming a micro-controller with extremely limited RAM. Reverse a string buffer in-place without allocating any extra memory.

Input: A single line containing the string s (no leading or trailing spaces).

Output: A single line containing s reversed.

Constraints: 1 <= |s| <= 10^5 s consists of printable ASCII characters excluding newline.

Optimization Scenarios (Two Pointers):
  • Try to solve this using strictly O(1) auxiliary space (in-place).
  • Optimize your approach to run in a single pass (O(N) time complexity) without nested loops.

stages.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
stages.statement:
Scenario: Network Packet Analysis
You are analyzing a stream of network packets. Find the length of the longest contiguous sequence of packets where no two packets have the same ID.

Input: Line 1: the string s (may be empty).

Output: A single integer: the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.

Constraints: 0 <= |s| <= 5 * 10^4 s consists of printable ASCII characters without spaces.

Optimization Scenarios (Two Pointers):
  • Try to solve this using strictly O(1) auxiliary space (in-place).
  • Optimize your approach to run in a single pass (O(N) time complexity) without nested loops.

stages.title: Trapping Rain Water
stages.statement:
Scenario: Civil Engineering
You are designing a city's drainage system. Given an elevation map representing the heights of buildings, calculate how much rainwater can be trapped between them after a storm.

Input: Line 1: integer n, the number of bars. Line 2: n space-separated non-negative integers, the bar heights.

Output: A single integer: the total units of trapped water.

Constraints: 1 <= n <= 2 * 10^4 0 <= height[i] <= 10^5

Optimization Scenarios (Two Pointers):
  • Try to solve this using strictly O(1) auxiliary space (in-place).
  • Optimize your approach to run in a single pass (O(N) time complexity) without nested loops.

stages.title: Move Zeroes
stages.statement:
Scenario: Disk Defragmentation
A storage disk represents empty blocks as 0. Shift all valid data to the front of the disk to create one contiguous block of free space at the end.

Input: Line 1: integer n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output: n space-separated integers with zeroes at the end.

Constraints: 1 <= n <= 10^4

Optimization Scenarios (Two Pointers):
  • Try to solve this using strictly O(1) auxiliary space (in-place).
  • Optimize your approach to run in a single pass (O(N) time complexity) without nested loops.

stages.title: Remove Element
stages.statement:
Scenario: Content Moderation
A cache block contains an array of user IDs. You must filter out all users who match a flagged ID in-place to save memory.

Input: Line 1: integer n and val. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output: Space-separated integers remaining after removing val.

Constraints: 0 <= n <= 100 0 <= val <= 100

Optimization Scenarios (Two Pointers):
  • Try to solve this using strictly O(1) auxiliary space (in-place).
  • Optimize your approach to run in a single pass (O(N) time complexity) without nested loops.

stages.title: Two Sum II
stages.statement:
Scenario: Ledger Reconciliation
You have a chronologically sorted array of transaction amounts. Find two transactions that exactly offset a known discrepancy target.

Input: Line 1: integer n. Line 2: n space-separated integers sorted ascending. Line 3: integer target.

Output: Two space-separated 1-indexed positions.

Constraints: 2 <= n <= 3 * 10^4

Optimization Scenarios (Two Pointers):
  • Try to solve this using strictly O(1) auxiliary space (in-place).
  • Optimize your approach to run in a single pass (O(N) time complexity) without nested loops.
